properties.note: Suggested field-sampling locations. Satellite observation is a screening tool; laboratory analysis of physical samples is required to confirm any interpretation.

properties.role_question: What is actually present at the point of strongest signal?
properties.rationale: Highest spectral anomaly in the event (RX 43707). The strongest signal gives laboratory analysis the best chance of identifying what is actually present.

properties.role_question: Has anything reached the protected asset yet?
properties.rationale: Nearest analysable water to Annaba Port power station, 378 m away. This is the measurement that answers whether the asset is affected yet.
expected_variables: Algal toxins if a bloom is suspected

properties.role_question: Where is the boundary, and is the event advancing?
properties.rationale: Edge of the event nearest the modelled drift direction (bearing 273deg). Sampling here tests whether the event is advancing and how sharp the front is.

properties.role_question: What does unaffected water in this body read today?
properties.rationale: Lowest-anomaly water at least 800 m offshore (RX 1.2). Without a same-day control, an absolute laboratory value from the event cannot be interpreted.
expected_variables: Same analyte suite as the event core, for direct comparison

properties.role_question: Where is the interpretation least certain?
properties.rationale: Marginal anomaly (RX between the 85th and 97th percentile) in shallow water, where bottom reflectance and suspended matter are hard to separate optically. A depth reading and a TSS sample here would resolve the ambiguity for the whole nearshore band.
